title: Nonthermal Dynamics of a One-dimensional Rydberg-atom Chain with Constraint Four-body Interactions
abstract: We investigate dynamics of a linear chain of Rydberg atoms driven by a constrained four-body interaction, where two neighboring atoms are excited simultaneously from the electronic ground state $|0\rangle$ to Rydberg state $|1\rangle$ only when their closest neighbors are in $|0\rangle$ state. By employing an ansatz for the many-body ground state, the low-energy Hamiltonian is given by a tridiagonal form. The many-body ground state energy, which scales linearly with the chain length $L$, is obtained analytically in the thermodynamic limit and agrees with the one of the exact diagonalization. Our model supports quantum many-body scar eigenstates that are nearly equally spaced energetically. The scar states overlap strongly with the basis state $|\mathbf{0}\rangle=|0\cdots 0\rangle$. We show that the overlap distribution is tilted by the state-dependent four-body interaction. This leads to non-ergodic dynamics, evidenced by the revival of the initial state. The four-body constrained model can be realized with Rydberg atoms in a Peierls array with alternating bond lengths, where atoms on the shorter and longer bonds experience Rydberg blockade and antiblockade, respectively. Our study provides a pathway to explore constrained non-ergodic dynamics with four-body interactions by combining the Rydberg blockade and antiblockade.

bite.hook: Constrained four-body interactions in Rydberg chains create quantum scars that prevent thermalization.
tldr: Modeled a 1D chain of Rydberg atoms with strict four-body excitation rules.
Analytically derived the ground-state Hamiltonian and computed scar states, matching exact diagonalization.
Discovered non-ergodic dynamics and periodic state revivals, realizable via alternating Rydberg blockade and antiblockade.
bite.whyItMatters: Preventing quantum systems from thermalizing and losing information is crucial for building robust quantum memories and simulators.
bite.eli5: Normally, adding energy to a row of atoms scrambles their information like melting ice into water. Here, strict interaction rules trap the system in a loop, repeatedly bouncing back to its original pattern.

glossary.shortDef: An atom excited to a very high principal quantum number, giving it huge size and strong interactions.
glossary.eli5Def: An atom puffed up like an oversized balloon, making it feel other atoms from far away.

glossary.shortDef: Special eigenstates in a chaotic quantum system that avoid thermalization and retain memory of initial states.
glossary.eli5Def: A few stubborn states in an otherwise chaotic system that refuse to melt into random noise.

glossary.shortDef: A mechanism where one excited Rydberg atom prevents nearby atoms from being excited due to strong shifts.
glossary.eli5Def: A rule where one atom getting excited pushes all its immediate neighbors away from being excited.

glossary.shortDef: Time evolution where a system fails to explore all accessible states and does not thermalize.
glossary.eli5Def: When a system never fully mixes up its parts, keeping its original structure over time.
